title: Amazon Rainforest Deforestation, Rondônia
headline: L-band cross-polarization drop tracks 187 km² of new fishbone deforestation corridors.
story: Rondônia in the southwestern Brazilian Amazon has historically experienced intensive 'fishbone' pattern clear-cutting along feeder roads. Dense triple-canopy rainforest scatters L-band radar waves heavily, producing high HV cross-polarization backscatter. When chainsaws and bulldozers strip the canopy away, volume scattering collapses immediately. Radar provides continuous alerts unaffected by equatorial cloud cover.
why_sar: Why radar sees through cloud and night: The Amazon basin is covered by thick convective rain clouds for months at a time. NISAR's L-band radar (24 cm wavelength) passes directly through clouds to measure forest structure.

story_steps.title: Intact Primary Rainforest Canopy
story_steps.description: L-band HV radar backscatter exhibits high uniform brightness from complex multi-layered canopy volume scattering.

story_steps.title: Corridor Logging & Encroachment
story_steps.description: New access trails cut into protected forest reserves show pronounced dark linear scars where trees were harvested.

story_steps.title: HV Drop Disturbance Alert
story_steps.description: OPERA DIST-ALERT vector polygons outline patches with greater than 4 dB backscatter attenuation.

story_steps.title: Fishbone Deforestation Front
story_steps.description: Systematic perpendicular clearing lots convert rich biodiversity corridors into cattle pasture.
